newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits seven-month low, ends down 50 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits seven-month low, ends down 50 cts.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures fell to a seven-month low and ended down 50 cents on Friday on aggressive selling of NYMEX crude futures, dealers said.
IPE April Brent last traded at $18.90 a barrel, 10 cents above the low of $18.80 and sharply below a range of $19.13 to $19.23 established in the last two hours of trade.
The last prompt futures fell below $19.00 was August 1 when they posted a $18.79 low.
"Hedge funds will see some buy signals at these numbers," a trader said. "But the whole market lacks confidence at the moment and the bounce on Monday may not be that strong."

Traders said a U.S. player's orders to sell WTI futures down as hard as possible triggered technical selling on IPE April Brent and pushed the contract decisively through the key $19.00 level in the last 10 minutes of business.
"The good volume seen at the lower numbers throughout the day, together with weaker U.S. gasoline, are negative signals and we could see continuing weakness," one player said.

IPE gas oil closed down $2 a tonne in dull activity in line with lower U.S. heating oil. IPE March gas oil last traded at $162.50 a tonne, 75 cents off the day's high, having moved in a range of $161.75 and $162.75 for the most of the afternoon.

NYMEX April crude was trading down 59 cents at $20.30 a barrel. March heating oil was off 1.53 cents at 54.50 cents a gallon after sliding below an eight month low for spot heat at 54.55. Gasoline was down 97 cents at 61.70 cents a gallon.
